name: MT-Bench
ability_definition: The ability to communicate information and ideas in writing so others will understand.

task_realism.reasoning: The Writing category (and partly Roleplay, Humanities, Extraction) includes plausible workplace-style prompts: draft a professional email, write a blog post, explain a concept, then revise under a follow-up constraint. The multi-turn revision step mirrors real editing requests. But half or more of the 80 questions are math, coding, reasoning and STEM items. Those exercise knowledge and problem solving rather than communicating ideas to a reader. The writing prompts are also short, generic briefs, not grounded in real organizational context or audiences.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: There are only two turns and no source materials, stakeholders or real audience. Nothing is at stake and there is no extended drafting or feedback loop. Grading uses a GPT-4 judge scoring 1-10, which agrees with humans above 80% but is a proxy reader with known biases toward verbosity, style and self-preference. The test is not whether a target reader actually understood the text. With about 10 writing items, the sample is tiny and fixed, so results are noisy and exposed to contamination. None of this resembles how written work is evaluated in practice.

construct_coverage.reasoning: Written Expression means clarity, organization, tone, grammar and audience-appropriate conveyance across many genres. MT-Bench devotes 1 of 8 categories to writing. Its headline score blends in math, coding and reasoning correctness, so it does not isolate the ability. Judge criteria (helpfulness, relevance, accuracy, depth, creativity, detail) only partly target reader comprehension. There is no coverage of long documents, technical reports, persuasion with evidence, or adapting to specific readers.

format_match.reasoning: Inputs are natural-language requests and outputs are free-form prose such as emails, posts, explanations and rewrites. These resemble real written artifacts, and there is no forced choice or toy format. However, outputs are short single responses rather than full-length documents. The numeric judge score is an artificial stand-in for reader feedback.

transferability_reasoning: MT-Bench asks for genuine free-form writing, including realistic briefs and revisions, so its format resembles real written work. However, writing is only a small slice of a composite score dominated by reasoning, math and coding. Grading is done by an LLM judge on a tiny, low-context prompt set, so the benchmark involves Written Expression without isolating it, and its transfer to workplace writing ability is modest.

2023.metric: Mean GPT-4-judge score on a 1-10 scale (overall MT-Bench score, not the Writing-category subscore)
2023.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce: typical college-educated professionals who write explanatory, persuasive and instructional text as part of their jobs (not professional writers or editors).
